A. Opening Page

Welcome to Chapter 4

In this chapter, you will learn how to read data in English. You will not only read paragraphs, but also read tables, bar charts, pie charts, line graphs, infographics, and survey results. Data can help us understand habits, trends, problems, and possible solutions.

Dalam bab ini, kamu akan belajar menghubungkan kemampuan Bahasa Inggris dengan literasi data. Kamu akan berlatih membaca data, menjelaskan grafik, membandingkan angka, menulis laporan, dan mempresentasikan hasil survei sederhana.

Learning Snapshot

Dalam chapter ini, kamu membaca data visual, menjelaskan tren, membandingkan kategori, dan menyimpulkan hasil data secara hati-hati.

  • Read visual data carefully
  • Describe trends and changes
  • Compare values responsibly
  • Write a mini-survey data report

Suasana pembelajaran Chapter 4: siswa mempelajari grafik dan kebiasaan belajar dalam kelas bernuansa kepulauan.

Why This Chapter Matters

In the digital age, data appears everywhere: school surveys, social media polls, health infographics, weather reports, internet usage charts, environmental reports, financial graphs, and scientific articles. If you can read data carefully, you can make better decisions.

English: Data can guide decisions, but careless interpretation can lead to wrong conclusions.
Artinya: Data dapat membimbing keputusan, tetapi penafsiran yang ceroboh dapat mengarah pada kesimpulan yang salah.

internet access for learning

Learning Goals

  1. Explain the purpose of information report and data commentary.
  2. Identify title, axis, category, percentage, legend, value, and source.
  3. Read tables, bar charts, pie charts, line graphs, and infographics.
  4. Describe trends and changes using accurate vocabulary.
  5. Use approximations such as about, around, nearly, and just over.
  6. Use comparative structures such as higher than, lower than, the highest, and compared with.
  7. Distinguish data description and data interpretation.
  8. Avoid overclaiming when interpreting data.
  9. Listen to a data presentation and complete notes.
  10. Conduct a simple mini-survey.
  11. Present survey data through a chart.
  12. Write an information report and data commentary.

C. Learning Approach

How You Will Learn

Genre-Based Approach

Building Knowledge of the Field, Modelling of the Text, Joint Construction, and Independent Construction.

Data Literacy-Based Learning

You read data, find patterns, compare values, interpret cautiously, and explain findings in English.

Inquiry-Based Learning

You ask survey questions, collect responses, organize data, analyze results, and present findings.

Project-Based Learning

You conduct a mini-survey, create a chart, write a report, and present it.

Mindful Learning

You read data carefully before making conclusions.

Meaningful & Joyful Learning

You connect data with study habits, coastal life, and learn through data hunt, survey challenge, and chart gallery.

English: Data literacy helps us understand what numbers show and what they do not show.
Artinya: Literasi data membantu kita memahami apa yang ditunjukkan angka dan apa yang tidak ditunjukkan angka.

English: A good survey begins with a clear question.
Artinya: Survei yang baik dimulai dengan pertanyaan yang jelas.

D. My Initial Understanding

What Do You Notice?

Lihat data berikut, lalu jawab dengan hati-hati. Jangan langsung menyimpulkan lebih dari yang ditunjukkan data.

Sample Learning Data 1: Daily Study Time among 30 Students

Study Time per DayNumber of Students
Less than 30 minutes5
30–60 minutes11
1–2 hours9
More than 2 hours5

Questions

  1. What category has the highest number?
  2. What category has the lowest number?
  3. Do most students study for more than two hours?
  4. What can you conclude carefully from the data?
  5. What can you not conclude from the data?

Useful Expressions

English ExpressionArti Bahasa Indonesia
I notice that…Saya memperhatikan bahwa…
The highest number is…Angka tertinggi adalah…
The lowest number is…Angka terendah adalah…

The data does not show why…Data tidak menunjukkan mengapa…

English: I notice that the largest group studies for 30–60 minutes per day. However, the data does not explain why students choose that study time.

F. Learning Input 1

What Is Information Report?

Infografis: perbedaan Information Report dan Data Commentary.

Definition

An information report is a factual text that presents information about a topic in a clear and organized way. It usually describes facts, categories, characteristics, or findings.

English: An information report presents factual information about a topic without telling a personal story.
Artinya: Information report menyajikan informasi faktual tentang sebuah topik tanpa menceritakan pengalaman pribadi.

Social Function

English: The purpose of an information report is to explain facts clearly and systematically.
Artinya: Tujuan information report adalah menjelaskan fakta secara jelas dan sistematis.

Where Can We Find Information Reports?

SourceExample
School survey reportReport about students’ study habits
Scientific reportReport about water quality or weather patterns
Company reportReport about customer behavior
Environmental reportReport about plastic waste reduction
Health reportReport about exercise or nutrition habits
Digital platform reportReport about internet use or screen time
Government/community reportReport about transportation access or public facilities

Structure of Information Report

PartFunction
TitleShows the topic of the report.
General StatementIntroduces the topic and context.
Description / FindingsPresents facts, categories, data, or observations.
Summary / ConclusionSummarizes the main findings.
Recommendation, if neededSuggests possible action based on findings.

Information Report vs Other Text Types

Text TypeMain PurposeExample
Information ReportPresents factual information about a topicA report about students’ study habits
News ItemReports a recent real eventStudents held a survey presentation
Discussion TextPresents arguments for and against an issueShould students reduce screen time?
Analytical ExpositionArgues that something is importantWhy data literacy is important
Data CommentaryDescribes and interprets dataThe chart shows that reading time increased.
G. Learning Input 2

What Is Data Commentary?

Definition and Social Function

A data commentary is a text that describes, explains, and interprets data shown in a chart, table, graph, or infographic. It helps readers understand patterns, trends, comparisons, and possible implications from data.

English: Data commentary helps readers understand patterns and possible meanings behind numbers.
Artinya: Data commentary membantu pembaca memahami pola dan kemungkinan makna di balik angka.

Describing Data vs Interpreting Data

TypeFunctionExampleArti
DescriptionTells what the data shows directly.The number increased from 20 to 35.Jumlahnya meningkat dari 20 menjadi 35.
InterpretationSuggests what the data may mean.This may suggest that more students prefer online learning support.Ini mungkin menunjukkan bahwa lebih banyak siswa menyukai dukungan pembelajaran online.
Cautious ConclusionAvoids overclaiming.However, the data does not explain the reason behind the increase.Namun, data tersebut tidak menjelaskan alasan di balik peningkatan itu.

Why Should We Avoid Overclaiming?

Weak / Overclaiming

English: All students love online learning because internet use increased.
Artinya: Semua siswa menyukai pembelajaran online karena penggunaan internet meningkat.

Better / Cautious Interpretation

English: The increase in internet use may indicate that more students use online resources, but the data does not show whether they enjoy online learning.
Artinya: Peningkatan penggunaan internet mungkin menunjukkan bahwa lebih banyak siswa menggunakan sumber online, tetapi data tersebut tidak menunjukkan apakah mereka menikmati pembelajaran online.

H. Learning Input 3

Understanding Visual Data

Infografis full: jenis data visual dan elemen pentingnya.

Types of Visual Data

Visual Data TypeDefinitionFunctionWhat to Look AtCommon MistakeExample Sentence + Arti
TableOrganizes information in rows and columns.Shows exact values clearly.Rows, columns, totals, category names.Reading only one number without comparing it.The table shows the number of students who prefer different study methods.
Tabel menunjukkan jumlah siswa yang menyukai metode belajar berbeda.
Bar ChartUses bars to compare categories.Shows which category is higher or lower.Axis, labels, bar height, scale.Ignoring the scale or axis.The bar chart shows that group study is more popular than individual study.
Grafik batang menunjukkan bahwa belajar kelompok lebih populer daripada belajar mandiri.
Pie ChartShows parts of a whole, usually in percentages.Shows proportions.Slices, percentage labels, total 100%.Forgetting that all slices represent 100%.The pie chart shows that 40% of students prefer videos as learning resources.
Diagram lingkaran menunjukkan bahwa 40% siswa menyukai video sebagai sumber belajar.
Line GraphShows changes over time.Shows trends, increases, decreases, and fluctuations.Time period, points, line direction, changes.Treating small changes as dramatic changes.The line graph shows a steady increase in internet use from Monday to Friday.
Grafik garis menunjukkan peningkatan stabil penggunaan internet dari Senin sampai Jumat.
InfographicCombines text, icons, images, and data.Explains information visually and attractively.Title, source, icons, numbers, captions.Believing an infographic without checking the source.The infographic summarizes students’ screen time and study habits.
Infografis merangkum waktu layar dan kebiasaan belajar siswa.
Survey ResultPresents answers from respondents.Shows opinions, habits, preferences, or experiences.Question, respondents, sample size, response options.Assuming a small sample represents everyone.The survey result shows that most respondents use the internet for learning.
Hasil survei menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar responden menggunakan internet untuk belajar.
Simple Scientific ReportPresents data from observation or experiment.Shows findings from investigation.Method, measurement, observation, result.Ignoring method and limitation.The report shows changes in plastic waste collected each week.
Laporan menunjukkan perubahan jumlah sampah plastik yang dikumpulkan setiap minggu.
Corporate or Organizational ReportPresents performance, activity, or outcome data.Informs stakeholders about progress or results.Indicator, period, comparison, summary.Reading it without context.The organization report shows a decline in single-use plastic after the campaign.
Laporan organisasi menunjukkan penurunan plastik sekali pakai setelah kampanye.

Elements of Visual Data

ElementMeaningExample
TitleThe name of the data displayStudents’ Study Habits
LabelThe name of each item or categoryReading, watching videos, group study
AxisHorizontal or vertical measurement lineX-axis shows days; Y-axis shows minutes
LegendExplanation of colors or symbolsBlue = boys, green = girls
CategoryGroup of dataStudy method, resource type
PercentagePart per 10035%
ValueNumber shown in data18 students
Sample sizeNumber of respondents30 students
SourceWhere the data comes fromSample Learning Data
TrendGeneral movementupward trend, downward trend
ComparisonDifference between categorieshigher than, lower than
ConclusionFinal statement based on dataMost students prefer videos
I. Learning Input 4

Reading Data Carefully

Infografis full: langkah membaca grafik dengan teliti.

Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Read the title. What is the data about?
  2. Check the source. Where does the data come from?
  3. Identify the categories. What groups are compared?
  4. Look at values and percentages. What numbers are shown?
  5. Find the pattern or trend. Does the data increase, decrease, fluctuate, or remain stable?
  6. Compare categories. Which category is higher, lower, or similar?
  7. Make a cautious interpretation. What may the data suggest?
  8. Know what cannot be concluded. What does the data not explain?

Checklist Before Concluding

What is the title?
What is being measured?
Who are the respondents?
How many respondents are there?
What period does the data cover?
What is the highest value?
What is the lowest value?
What cannot be concluded?

2. Approximations

Approximations are used when numbers are not exact or when we want to describe data naturally.

English: Approximations help us describe data without sounding too rigid.
Artinya: Approximation membantu kita menjelaskan data tanpa terdengar terlalu kaku.

Information Report and Data Commentary

Infografis full: Students’ Study Habits Survey.

Reading Text 1 • Sample Learning Text

Students’ Study Habits Survey

Source Note: Sample Learning Data

1. Data Display

Daily Study TimeNumber of Students
Less than 30 minutes5
30–60 minutes11
1–2 hours9
More than 2 hours5

2. Information Report

This report presents the result of a mini-survey about daily study time among 30 Grade XII students. The survey asked students how long they usually study outside regular school hours in one day.

The data shows four categories of study time. The largest group, 11 students, reported that they study for 30–60 minutes per day. The second largest group, 9 students, reported that they study for 1–2 hours per day. Two categories had the same number of students: 5 students studied for less than 30 minutes, and 5 students studied for more than 2 hours per day.

Overall, most students in this sample study between 30 minutes and 2 hours per day. The data suggests that many students have a moderate daily study routine. However, the survey does not explain the quality of their study, the subjects they study, or the reasons behind their study time.

3. Terjemahan Bahasa Indonesia

Laporan ini menyajikan hasil survei mini tentang waktu belajar harian 30 siswa kelas XII. Survei tersebut menanyakan berapa lama siswa biasanya belajar di luar jam sekolah dalam satu hari.

Data menunjukkan empat kategori waktu belajar. Kelompok terbesar, yaitu 11 siswa, melaporkan bahwa mereka belajar selama 30–60 menit per hari. Kelompok terbesar kedua, yaitu 9 siswa, melaporkan bahwa mereka belajar selama 1–2 jam per hari. Dua kategori memiliki jumlah siswa yang sama: 5 siswa belajar kurang dari 30 menit, dan 5 siswa belajar lebih dari 2 jam per hari.

Secara keseluruhan, sebagian besar siswa dalam sampel ini belajar antara 30 menit sampai 2 jam per hari. Data tersebut menunjukkan bahwa banyak siswa memiliki rutinitas belajar harian sedang. Namun, survei tersebut tidak menjelaskan kualitas belajar mereka, mata pelajaran yang mereka pelajari, atau alasan di balik waktu belajar mereka.

4. Data Commentary

The bar chart would show that the 30–60 minute category is the highest, with 11 students. The 1–2 hour category is slightly lower, with 9 students. The categories “less than 30 minutes” and “more than 2 hours” are equal, with 5 students each.

This may indicate that most respondents do not study for extremely short or extremely long periods. However, the data is limited because it only includes 30 students and does not measure learning outcomes.

regular school hoursjam sekolah reguler
categorykategori
moderatesedang
learning outcomeshasil belajar
limited datadata terbatas

Reading Text 2 • Sample Learning Text

Internet Use for Learning in a Coastal School

Source Note: Sample Learning Data

1. Data Display

DayAverage Internet Use for Learning
Monday45 minutes
Tuesday50 minutes
Wednesday70 minutes
Thursday65 minutes
Friday80 minutes

2. Information Report

This report presents sample learning data about students’ average daily internet use for learning during five school days. The data was collected from 30 Grade XII students in a coastal school context.

On Monday, students used the internet for learning for an average of 45 minutes. The number rose slightly to 50 minutes on Tuesday. On Wednesday, it increased sharply to 70 minutes. The average time decreased slightly to 65 minutes on Thursday, but then reached the highest point on Friday at 80 minutes.

Overall, the data shows an upward trend from Monday to Friday, although there was a small decline on Thursday. This may suggest that students used more online resources toward the end of the week. However, the data does not show whether the increase was caused by homework, exam preparation, teacher instructions, or personal study habits.

3. Terjemahan Bahasa Indonesia

Laporan ini menyajikan data pembelajaran contoh tentang rata-rata penggunaan internet harian untuk belajar selama lima hari sekolah. Data dikumpulkan dari 30 siswa kelas XII dalam konteks sekolah pesisir.

Pada hari Senin, siswa menggunakan internet untuk belajar rata-rata selama 45 menit. Jumlah tersebut naik sedikit menjadi 50 menit pada hari Selasa. Pada hari Rabu, jumlahnya meningkat tajam menjadi 70 menit. Rata-rata waktu menurun sedikit menjadi 65 menit pada hari Kamis, tetapi kemudian mencapai titik tertinggi pada hari Jumat, yaitu 80 menit.

Secara keseluruhan, data menunjukkan tren naik dari Senin sampai Jumat, meskipun ada penurunan kecil pada hari Kamis. Hal ini mungkin menunjukkan bahwa siswa menggunakan lebih banyak sumber online menjelang akhir minggu. Namun, data tidak menunjukkan apakah peningkatan tersebut disebabkan oleh tugas rumah, persiapan ujian, instruksi guru, atau kebiasaan belajar pribadi.

4. Data Commentary

The line graph would show a general upward trend in internet use for learning. The average increased from 45 minutes on Monday to 80 minutes on Friday. The sharpest increase occurred between Tuesday and Wednesday, when internet use rose from 50 to 70 minutes.

Although there was a slight decline on Thursday, the trend continued upward on Friday. This could suggest that online learning resources became more important later in the week, but further information is needed to explain the reason.

Reading Text 3 • Sample Learning Text

Plastic Bottle Use and Refill Habit at School

Source Note: Sample Learning Data

1. Data Display

Drinking Water HabitPercentage
Bring reusable bottle45%
Buy bottled water30%
Use school refill station15%
Rarely drink water at school10%

2. Information Report

This report presents sample learning data about drinking water habits among 40 students at school. The survey focused on whether students bring reusable bottles, buy bottled water, use a refill station, or rarely drink water at school.

The largest percentage, 45%, represents students who bring reusable bottles. The second largest group, 30%, buys bottled water at school. Around 15% of students use the school refill station, while 10% rarely drink water at school.

The data shows that reusable bottles are the most common option among the respondents. However, a significant number of students still buy bottled water. This may indicate that plastic bottle use remains an issue. The data does not explain why students choose bottled water, so further questions are needed.

3. Terjemahan Bahasa Indonesia

Laporan ini menyajikan data pembelajaran contoh tentang kebiasaan minum air 40 siswa di sekolah. Survei berfokus pada apakah siswa membawa botol minum isi ulang, membeli air kemasan, menggunakan stasiun isi ulang sekolah, atau jarang minum air di sekolah.

Persentase terbesar, 45%, menunjukkan siswa yang membawa botol minum isi ulang. Kelompok terbesar kedua, 30%, membeli air kemasan di sekolah. Sekitar 15% siswa menggunakan stasiun isi ulang sekolah, sedangkan 10% jarang minum air di sekolah.

Data menunjukkan bahwa botol isi ulang adalah pilihan paling umum di antara responden. Namun, sejumlah siswa yang cukup banyak masih membeli air kemasan. Hal ini mungkin menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan botol plastik masih menjadi masalah. Data tersebut tidak menjelaskan mengapa siswa memilih air kemasan, sehingga pertanyaan lanjutan diperlukan.

4. Data Commentary

The pie chart would show that nearly half of the respondents bring reusable bottles. In comparison, 30% buy bottled water, which is lower than the reusable bottle category but still significant. The refill station category accounts for just 15%, while the smallest group, 10%, rarely drinks water at school.

This may suggest that the school could improve access to refill stations or encourage students to bring reusable bottles. However, the chart does not show students’ reasons or the availability of drinking water facilities.

Reading Text 4 • Sample Learning Text

Preferred Learning Resources among Grade XII Students

Source Note: Sample Learning Data

1. Data Display

Learning ResourceNumber of Students
Online videos13
Printed books7
Teacher notes6
Group discussion4
Podcasts2

2. Information Report

This report presents sample learning data about preferred learning resources among 32 Grade XII students. The survey asked students to choose the resource they use most often when studying.

The most popular resource was online videos, chosen by 13 students. Printed books were chosen by 7 students, while teacher notes were chosen by 6 students. Group discussion was selected by 4 students, and podcasts were the least common choice, selected by only 2 students.

Overall, the data shows that online videos were more popular than other learning resources in this sample. This may indicate that visual and audio materials are useful for many students. However, the data does not show whether online videos are more effective than books, notes, discussion, or podcasts.

3. Terjemahan Bahasa Indonesia

Laporan ini menyajikan data pembelajaran contoh tentang sumber belajar yang disukai oleh 32 siswa kelas XII. Survei meminta siswa memilih sumber yang paling sering mereka gunakan saat belajar.

Sumber paling populer adalah video online, dipilih oleh 13 siswa. Buku cetak dipilih oleh 7 siswa, sedangkan catatan guru dipilih oleh 6 siswa. Diskusi kelompok dipilih oleh 4 siswa, dan podcast adalah pilihan paling tidak umum, hanya dipilih oleh 2 siswa.

Secara keseluruhan, data menunjukkan bahwa video online lebih populer daripada sumber belajar lain dalam sampel ini. Hal ini mungkin menunjukkan bahwa materi visual dan audio berguna bagi banyak siswa. Namun, data tersebut tidak menunjukkan apakah video online lebih efektif daripada buku, catatan, diskusi, atau podcast.

4. Data Commentary

The table shows that online videos had the highest number of responses, with 13 out of 32 students. This is nearly twice as many as printed books, which were chosen by 7 students. Teacher notes were slightly lower than printed books, with 6 students.

Podcasts had the lowest number, with only 2 students. The data may suggest that students prefer visual learning resources, but it cannot prove that videos produce better learning outcomes.

Students’ Study Habits and Internet Use

Natural TTS Browser Mode

Buka Script Listening / Audio Script for TTS

Presenter: Good morning, everyone. Today, I will present the findings of our mini-survey about students’ study habits and internet use. The survey involved 30 Grade XII students. All data in this presentation is used for learning purposes.

First, we asked students about their daily study time. The data shows that 11 students study for 30 to 60 minutes per day. Nine students study for one to two hours per day. Five students study for less than 30 minutes, and another five students study for more than two hours.

This means that the largest group studies for 30 to 60 minutes per day. The second largest group studies for one to two hours. The data may indicate that many students have a moderate study routine. However, it does not show the quality of their study.

Second, we asked students about their internet use for learning. On Monday, the average was 45 minutes. On Tuesday, it increased slightly to 50 minutes. On Wednesday, it rose sharply to 70 minutes. On Thursday, it declined slightly to 65 minutes. Finally, on Friday, it reached the highest point at 80 minutes.

Overall, the line graph shows an upward trend in internet use for learning. Compared with Monday, Friday had a much higher average. This could suggest that students used more online resources toward the end of the week. However, further information is needed to explain why this happened.

Student Questioner: Excuse me. Can we conclude that students became more diligent on Friday?

Presenter: That is a good question. We should be careful. The data only shows internet use for learning. It does not show motivation, study quality, or learning results.

Teacher Facilitator: Good answer. When we present data, we must describe it accurately and interpret it responsibly. Numbers can help us understand patterns, but they do not explain everything by themselves.

Presenter: Thank you. In conclusion, the survey shows that many students study for a moderate amount of time and that internet use for learning increased during the week. However, the data is limited because it only includes 30 students and does not explain the reasons behind the trend.

Terjemahan Script

Presenter: Selamat pagi, semuanya. Hari ini, saya akan mempresentasikan temuan survei mini kami tentang kebiasaan belajar dan penggunaan internet siswa. Survei ini melibatkan 30 siswa kelas XII. Semua data dalam presentasi ini digunakan untuk tujuan pembelajaran.

Pertama, kami menanyakan waktu belajar harian siswa. Data menunjukkan bahwa 11 siswa belajar selama 30 sampai 60 menit per hari. Sembilan siswa belajar selama satu sampai dua jam per hari. Lima siswa belajar kurang dari 30 menit, dan lima siswa lainnya belajar lebih dari dua jam.

Data tersebut mungkin menunjukkan bahwa banyak siswa memiliki rutinitas belajar sedang. Namun, data tersebut tidak menunjukkan kualitas belajar mereka.

Kedua, kami menanyakan penggunaan internet untuk belajar. Pada hari Senin rata-ratanya 45 menit, naik sedikit pada Selasa, naik tajam pada Rabu, turun sedikit pada Kamis, lalu mencapai 80 menit pada Jumat.

Kesimpulannya, penggunaan internet untuk belajar meningkat selama minggu tersebut. Namun, data ini terbatas dan tidak menjelaskan alasan di balik tren tersebut.

O. Speaking Section

Data Talk and Mini Presentation

Siswa mempresentasikan data visual dan kesimpulan hati-hati di kelas.

Speaking Focus

Gunakan bahasa Inggris untuk menjelaskan grafik secara singkat, menyebutkan nilai tertinggi/terendah, membandingkan data, dan memberi cautious interpretation.

  • The chart shows…
  • The highest category is…
  • Compared with…, …
  • The data may suggest…

Speaking Activities

Data Talk

Choose one chart and explain it in three sentences.

Pair Interpretation

Ask and answer questions about highest, lowest, and missing information.

Chart Description Practice

Describe a bar chart, pie chart, or line graph using accurate language.

Survey Interview

Interview classmates politely and record anonymous answers.

Mini Presentation

Present findings in 1–2 minutes.

Gallery Walk Presentation

Move around, view classmates’ charts, and ask questions.

Model Conversations

1. Describing a Bar Chart

Student A: What does the bar chart show?
Apa yang ditunjukkan grafik batang tersebut?

Student B: It shows students’ daily study time.
Grafik tersebut menunjukkan waktu belajar harian siswa.

Student A: Which category is the highest?
Kategori mana yang tertinggi?

Student B: The 30–60 minute category is the highest, with 11 students.
Kategori 30–60 menit adalah yang tertinggi, dengan 11 siswa.

2. Survey Interview

Student A: I am conducting a mini-survey about learning resources. May I ask you a question?
Saya sedang melakukan survei mini tentang sumber belajar. Bolehkah saya bertanya?

Student B: Sure.
Tentu.

Student A: Which learning resource do you use most often: videos, books, teacher notes, group discussion, or podcasts?
Sumber belajar mana yang paling sering kamu gunakan: video, buku, catatan guru, diskusi kelompok, atau podcast?

3. Explaining a Pie Chart

Student A: The pie chart shows drinking water habits at school.
Diagram lingkaran menunjukkan kebiasaan minum air di sekolah.

Student B: What is the largest percentage?
Berapa persentase terbesar?

Student A: The largest percentage is 45%. It represents students who bring reusable bottles.
Persentase terbesar adalah 45%. Itu mewakili siswa yang membawa botol isi ulang.

4. Cautious Interpretation

Teacher: You said the chart proves that students learn better with videos. Is that conclusion safe?
Kamu mengatakan bahwa grafik membuktikan siswa belajar lebih baik dengan video. Apakah kesimpulan itu aman?

Student: Maybe not. The chart only shows preference, not learning results.
Mungkin tidak. Grafik hanya menunjukkan preferensi, bukan hasil belajar.

P. Writing Section

How to Write an Information Report and Data Commentary

  1. Choose a Survey Topic. Pilih topik aman dan relevan: study time, learning resources, reading habit, screen time, plastic bottle use, transportation to school.
  2. Write Survey Questions. Pertanyaan harus jelas, sederhana, dan tidak terlalu pribadi.
  3. Collect Responses. Minimal 15 teman, anonim, tanpa data sensitif.
  4. Organize Data in a Table. Susun option, number of responses, percentage.
  5. Choose a Suitable Chart. Bar chart untuk kategori, pie chart untuk persentase, line graph untuk perubahan waktu.
  6. Describe the Chart. Gunakan deskripsi faktual.
  7. Identify Highest and Lowest Values. Jelaskan kategori tertinggi dan terendah.
  8. Make Comparisons. Gunakan higher than, lower than, compared with.
  9. Use Approximations. Gunakan about, around, nearly, just over, just under.
  10. Write Cautious Interpretation. Gunakan may suggest, could indicate, the data does not show why.
  11. Write a Conclusion. Ringkas temuan dan sebutkan keterbatasan data.

English: Survey answers should be collected ethically and anonymously.
Artinya: Jawaban survei sebaiknya dikumpulkan secara etis dan anonim.

Report Structure Template

Title: ___________________________

Source Note: This report uses data from __________________________.

General Statement: This report presents the result of a mini-survey about __________________________. The survey involved __________ respondents.

Findings: The highest category is __________, with __________ respondents. The lowest category is __________, with __________ respondents. Compared with __________, __________ is higher/lower.

Data Commentary: The data may suggest that __________. However, the data does not show __________________________.

Cautious Conclusion: In conclusion, __________________________. Further information is needed to __________________________.

Joint Construction Example

Students’ Preferred Study Time

Preferred Study TimeNumber of Students
Morning4
Afternoon7
Evening12
Late night5

This report presents the result of a mini-survey about students’ preferred study time. The survey involved 28 Grade XII students and asked them when they usually prefer to study outside regular school hours.

The data shows that evening is the most popular study time, chosen by 12 students. Afternoon study was chosen by 7 students, while late-night study was chosen by 5 students. Morning study had the lowest number, with only 4 students.

Compared with morning study, evening study was three times higher. This may indicate that many students prefer studying after school activities and personal routines. However, the data does not explain whether evening study is more effective than other study times.

In conclusion, the survey shows that evening is the most common preferred study time in this sample. Further information is needed to understand the reasons behind this preference and its effect on learning outcomes.

Q. Mini Lab

Data Detective Lab: From Survey to Insight

Mini Lab Snapshot

Siswa melakukan survei kecil secara sopan, anonim, dan aman, lalu mengolah data menjadi tabel, grafik, dan data commentary.

  • Choose a safe topic
  • Collect at least 15 responses
  • Create a chart
  • Present findings clearly

Mini Lab: siswa mengumpulkan data survei dengan sopan dan anonim.

Purpose: You will collect simple data, present it in a chart, and write a data commentary in English.

Important Ethics Reminder

Do not ask about sensitive personal data such as home address, family income, religion, ethnicity, health condition, or political opinion.

English: A student survey should be safe, respectful, and anonymous.
Artinya: Survei siswa harus aman, santun, dan anonim.

Steps

  1. Choose one survey topic close to students’ life.
  2. Write 3–5 survey questions.
  3. Collect answers from at least 15 classmates.
  4. Make a data table.
  5. Turn the data into a simple chart.
  6. Identify the highest and lowest values.
  7. Find patterns or trends.
  8. Write one paragraph of information report.
  9. Write one paragraph of data commentary.
  10. Write a cautious conclusion.
  11. Present the findings in 2–3 minutes.

R. Grammar and Language Practice

Practice

Practice 1: Vocabulary for Trends

  1. The number of students using reusable bottles went from 12 to 20. It _____.
    A. increased B. declined C. remained stable D. plateaued E. disappeared
  2. The percentage stayed at 40% for three weeks. It _____.
    A. fluctuated B. remained stable C. dropped sharply D. peaked E. fell dramatically
  3. Internet use rose and fell several times during the week. It _____.
    A. fluctuated B. plateaued C. declined steadily D. stayed constant E. stopped

Practice 2: Approximations

  1. __________ 50% of students use online videos for learning.
  2. __________ half of the respondents prefer studying in the evening.
  3. The percentage is __________ 30%, but not exactly 30%.
  4. __________ 10 students chose podcasts.
  5. The result is __________ 25%, slightly higher than one-fourth.

Suggested: about, nearly, around, fewer than, slightly above.

Practice 3: Comparative Structures

  1. Videos: 13 students. Podcasts: 2 students.
  2. Evening study: 12 students. Morning study: 4 students.
  3. Bottled water: 30%. Reusable bottle: 45%.
  4. Monday internet use: 45 minutes. Friday internet use: 80 minutes.

Practice 4: Avoiding Overclaiming

  1. All students love online videos because 13 students chose them.
  2. Students who study at night always get better scores.
  3. Reusable bottles solve all plastic waste problems at school.
  4. Internet use increased, so students became smarter.
  5. Podcasts are useless because only 2 students chose them.
Kunci Jawaban dan Suggested Answers

Practice 1: 1 A, 2 B, 3 A.

Practice 3 Suggested: Online videos were more popular than podcasts. Evening study was three times higher than morning study. Reusable bottles had a higher percentage than bottled water. Compared with Monday, Friday had higher internet use.

Practice 4 Example: The data may suggest that online videos are popular among the respondents, but it does not show that all students love them.

True / False with Reasons

No.StatementTrue/FalseReason
1A line graph is useful for showing changes over time.
2A pie chart usually shows parts of a whole.
3Data commentary should avoid overclaiming.
4“About” can be used for approximation.
5A small survey always represents all students.
6“The highest” is used to describe the largest value.
7The source of data is not important.
8Data can show patterns but may not explain reasons.
9“Compared with” is useful for comparison.
10A cautious conclusion is weaker because it is dishonest.
Answer Key True/False
  1. True — line graphs show changes over time.
  2. True — pie charts show proportions.
  3. True — overclaiming can mislead readers.
  4. True — about means sekitar.
  5. False — a small survey has limited representation.
  6. True — the highest describes the largest value.
  7. False — source helps readers evaluate reliability.
  8. True — data may show what happens, not why it happens.
  9. True — compared with shows comparison.
  10. False — cautious conclusion is responsible and honest.

T. Final Project

Mini-Survey Data Report

You will conduct a mini-survey among your classmates about a lifestyle or study habit. Then, you will organize the data, create a chart, write an information report, write a data commentary, and present your findings.

Project Requirements

  1. one safe and relevant survey topic;
  2. 3–5 survey questions;
  3. at least 15 respondents;
  4. anonymous responses;
  5. one data table;
  6. at least one chart;
  7. one information report;
  8. one data commentary;
  9. at least 10 trend/change vocabulary items;
  10. at least 8 approximation expressions;
  11. at least 8 comparative structures;
  12. one cautious conclusion;
  13. one limitation statement;
  14. a short oral presentation.

Suggested Topics

Daily study time
Preferred study method
Internet use for learning
Most used learning resources
Reading habit
Sleep and study schedule
Exercise habit
Drinking water habit
Plastic bottle use
Screen time
Transportation to school
Interest in digital skills
